79915.subject: How to Use Claude Opus 5.5: The Complete Guide 📚
79915.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/how-to-use-claude-opus-5-5

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
Anthropic has finally made frontier-level AI cheaper, and most teams will still end up paying close to full price.
Claude Opus 5.5, released on September 22, 2026, is Anthropic’s new default model. Anthropic says it matches Claude Fable 5.1 on most work, writes output more than 30% faster than Opus 5, and costs about 40% less to run. Of course, that last number holds only for typical workloads at default settings, a condition most teams will definitely miss.
Token prices fell only 20%, to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. The rest of the savings comes from the model using fewer tokens per task, and it only does that if you set it up right. Opus 5.5 is also now the default model in Claude Code on all paid plans and ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
An early tester used Opus 5.5 to audit and fix a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours, a job that took Opus 5 more than 20. In Anthropic’s earnings-research test, 16 of 18 Opus 5.5 reports contained no invented figures or quotes. Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 didn’t manage a single clean report. Quantium cut one coding task from 38 prompts over 4 days to 11 prompts over 3 hours. Not too shabby! 👏
Opus 5.5 to explaining camera focus by building an interactive lens lab. Source: Ryan Sael via X
Of course, you won’t get those results with habits carried over from older models. Three key mistakes account for most of the waste:
Running it at max effort. At max, Artificial Analysis measured about 119,000 output tokens per task, 1.6 times as many as Opus 5, so the cost per task ends up the same as Opus 5. The 40% saving thus disappears. Medium, the default, already matches or beats Opus 5 at high on Anthropic’s coding and knowledge-work evaluations. Use it.
Keeping old prompt habits. In Anthropic’s tests, deleting “think carefully” lines made replies start sooner with no clear loss of quality. Requests for the model’s chain of thought are now blocked, and since September 24 the API also bills you for those refusals.
Trusting unattended runs to finish. On long tasks, Opus 5.5 sometimes ends a turn with a progress report. An agent loop that reads that report as “done” stops halfway through the migration you left running overnight. Keep this in mind.
There’s a quality gap to manage as well. In Sonar’s evaluation, Opus 5.5’s code had 44% more concurrency problems per line than Opus 5’s. In Endor Labs’ testing, only 33.5% of its fixes passed the security checks once memorized answers were excluded. If your checks don’t target those weak spots, you’ll definitely ship them.

79910.body:
Modern Alchemy 

Автор: Jake Bartolo


Автор: Jake Bartolo

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/house-doesnt-need-cheat-jake-bartolo-wxyhe?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3B5NnXeXn0SYa77yx%2B3TEjfg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1NftgkbwQupcs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mumf2qn0~qw-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mumf2qn0-qw
  
In July 2025, Congress passed the GENIUS Act, establishing the first comprehensive US federal framework for payment stablecoins, and most of the industry celebrated. To understand what it builds, it helps to start with a notorious gangster. Meyer Lansky spent fifty years moving money where the state could not see it. Along the way, he worked with US Naval Intelligence and watched his Havana partners go to work for the CIA. The law written to stop him now governs every bank account you hold. The Justice Department that pursued Lansky later took surveillance-grade software from its owner by fraud, and a copy of it went to an Israeli spymaster. GENIUS carries the same ambitions onto programmable dollars. This piece builds on the research and insights of Dr. Jack Kruse, following the thread from Lansky’s counting room to the stablecoin. The craps table Maier Suchowljansky was born in Grodno, in the Russian Empire, in 1902, arriving on New York’s Lower East Side in 1911. Watching street craps as a boy, he worked out that the house wins without cheating because the odds already favour it. He built a career on that idea. He ran with Benjamin “Bugsy” Siegel (his childhood friend and future Las Vegas casino builder) and Charles “Lucky” Luciano (Italian-American crime boss and head of the National Crime Syndicate) when Jewish and Italian gangs mostly kept apart. Prohibition made them rich. Lansky became the organiser behind the violence. He kept the numbers in his head and later ran his casinos straight, because an honest casino with a house edge makes more over time than a crooked one. The press called him the mob’s accountant. The Navy’s gangsters During WW2, on 9 February 1942, the liner Normandie burned and capsized at her New York pier while being converted into a troopship. Sabotage was suspected. U-boats were sinking ships off the east coast, and Naval Intelligence could get nothing from dockworkers on a waterfront the mob controlled. So the Navy went to the mob, and Lansky was the go-between with Lucky Luciano, who was then in prison. Luciano’s people secured the docks and later helped with intelligence for the invasion of Sicily. In 1946, Luciano was released and deported to Italy. The Navy destroyed most of its records.
